name: Caucasus
front_desc: the coast and the north Caucasus

background: A long dispute on the Black Sea coast has turned into open war. Russia has moved a combined-arms army group and its southern air regiments up the coast road, from Krymsk and Gelendzhik through Sochi into Abkhazia, and its columns are pushing on toward the Georgian airbase at Senaki. The army group is covered by one of the densest air-defence networks in the region and by modern fighters.

A US-led coalition has answered Georgia's request for help. The carrier USS Stennis and her air wing operate from the eastern Black Sea; U.S. Air Force squadrons fly from Senaki, Kutaisi and Kobuleti. You fly with the Navy's carrier air wing or with the Air Force, as part of a joint air campaign.

The mountains close the interior, so the coast road is the only way through. The war will be settled on that road, base by base. Each airfield taken pushes the front back, brings the next one into range and puts the enemy's air defences, fuel and depots in the way. Nobody on either side is trying to march on a capital.
3.intent: Coalition command's intent: break the enemy's air defences and supply along the coast, support the ground force as it takes the airfields one by one, and hold what we take until the next push is ready. Sukhumi first, then Gudauta and Sochi, then Gelendzhik and Krymsk. Every day the war is planned and the packages go out. Yours is the one you fly yourself.

now.Offensive: The advance is moving. Our ground force at the front outweighs Russia's here, and the air campaign is keeping it that way.
now.Consolidating: We hold what we took. The next push waits for the takeover to finish; use the time to hit supply and air defence.
now.Holding: The front is not moving. Our ground force at the contested sector is not yet strong enough to attack; close air support and supply strikes decide the next move.
now.Under pressure: Russia is gaining ground on our side of the line. Hold the sector in front of our airfields.
now.Last stand: The final objective is next. Take it and the war is decided.
now.Defeat: Two of our airfields are gone and the front has collapsed. The campaign is lost.
now.Counter-force: A fresh Russian force has arrived and is counter-attacking the airfield we just took. Beat it and the war is won.
now.Ceasefire: Russia has asked for talks and the guns have gone quiet along the coast. The campaign is won.

beats.back_blue: {base} is ours again, though its defences are gone.

beats.lose: The front has collapsed. With two of our airfields lost the coalition withdraws, and the campaign is lost.
beats.fall_ab_sukhumi: Sukhumi is ours. Georgian and coalition troops hold the airfield; the first step up the coast road is taken.
beats.fall_ab_gudauta: Gudauta falls. Abkhazia is behind us and the road to Sochi is open.

beats.fall_ab_gelen: Gelendzhik is ours. The Black Sea coast opens up ahead of the column.
beats.fall_ab_krymsk: Krymsk falls. The last Russian air base on the coast is in coalition hands.

background: A militia calling itself the Coastal Republic Army (CRA) has seized the coastal cities from Sukhumi to Sochi and is pushing toward the Georgian airbase at Senaki. It fights with old Soviet armor and a few obsolete jets under old but working SAM batteries, museum pieces that somebody across the border has kept in repair. It is resupplied by night across the border, so it never quite runs dry.

A US-led coalition has answered Georgia's request for help. The carrier USS Stennis and her air wing operate from the eastern Black Sea; U.S. Air Force squadrons fly from Senaki, Kutaisi and Kobuleti. You fly with the Navy's carrier air wing or with the Air Force, as part of a joint air campaign.

The mountains close the interior, so the coast road is the only way through. The campaign is a push along that road, city by city, against an enemy that is outgunned but does not give up ground easily.
1.intent: Coalition command's intent: keep the militia's supply and air defences under pressure, support the ground force as it retakes the coastal cities, and hold what we retake. Sukhumi first, then Gudauta, then Sochi. Every day the war is planned and the packages go out. Yours is the one you fly yourself.

now.Defeat: Two of our airfields are gone and the front has collapsed. The campaign is lost.

title: Operation IRON TIDE
background:
After months of border incidents and a collapsed ceasefire, the Northern Federation's Southern Military District crossed the frontier in force. Its armored columns are pushing south along the Black Sea coast toward the Georgian airbase at Senaki, supported by air regiments at Sukhumi, Gudauta, Sochi and across the Kuban, and covered by a layered air-defence network.

A coalition task force has answered the request for assistance. The USS Stennis carrier air wing operates from the eastern Black Sea; U.S. Air Force squadrons operate from Senaki, Kutaisi and Kobuleti. You fly with the Navy's Tomcat community or with the Air Force, as part of a joint air campaign.

Coalition command's intent is plain: stop the armored advance, win control of the air, take the enemy air-defence network apart, and then strike the headquarters and logistics that keep the offensive moving. Every day the war is planned; every day the packages go out. Yours is the one you fly yourself.

climate.source: Sochi monthly normals: sunshine hours (NOAA 1961-1990) and days with precipitation (Pogoda.ru.net), as published in Wikipedia 'Climate of Sochi'. sun_frac = sunshine hours / possible daylight hours at 43.6N; rain_frac = precipitation days / days in month. wind_ms and fog are hand-tuned, not measured.
